newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish pulp producers may raise prices - media.
newsitem.headline: Finnish pulp producers may raise prices - media.

text.p: Finnish forest industry companies may follow North-American competitors and raise pulp prices if possible price hikes by U.S. Georgia-Pacific and Stone Container go through, Finnish media reported on Monday.

"It must be kept in mind that these price hikes are based on curtailing of production. Although there would be a temporary shortage of pulp, there is no boom in sight for pulp demand," Finnish Metsa-Botnia's marketing chief, Jyrki Yrjo-Koskinen, was quoted as saying in the daily Kauppalehti.
Finnish pulp producers have said that pulp prices have now bottomed out and that the curtailing of production in North-America would have a positive effect on the price development of pulp.
Kauppalehti said Georgia-Pacific and Stone were planning to raise the price of northern long-fibre pulp to $580 per tonne in May from the current $520 per tonne.
